founding_year.basis: founded 2000 as Benchmark Capital Europe; the firm's own post of 2014-04-01: 'Balderton has been investing since 2000, when it was Benchmark Capital Europe, before rebranding in 2007'; Benchmark Europe I closed in May 2000 (Light Reading).

history.value: Balderton Capital was founded in London in 2000 as Benchmark Capital Europe, by partners including Barry Maloney, George Coelho and Mark Evans, and became independent under its own name in 2007. It became known for early bets on Betfair, MySQL, Yoox, Revolut and Depop. In 2024 it raised $1.3 billion across its ninth early stage fund and its second growth fund.
history.basis: founding and independence: VentureBeat 2007-06-07 and the firm's post of 2014-04-01; founders: Globoforce's 2013 registration statement ('Mr. Maloney is a General Partner and a founder of Balderton Capital'), the benchmark.com Europe desk pages from 2000 (Maloney, Coelho, Evans, Archambeau) and the founding members of the manager on 2004-02-12 (Companies House OC306910: Coelho, Evans, Maloney); the named bets are portfolio companies on this page; 2024 funds: the firm's post of 2024-08-12 ($615M Early Stage Fund IX, $685M Growth Fund II). Moved here from the page: the fund ladder since Benchmark Europe I; the track record on this page includes the 2000 to 2007 companies of the Benchmark years (decisions.md D2) and leaves out two companies the firm controlled outright, Alphyra and NASN (R2).

investment_concept.value: “Europe's leading venture firm focused exclusively on backing European-founded tech companies.”
investment_concept.basis: The firm's own statement, verbatim from the homepage title tag, read 2026-09-26 (the homepage has no h1 headline; its h2 reads 'Two decades. Hundreds of Europe's best founders'). A closing period and straight quotes are the only edits. The meta description is the competing line ('In the two decades since our founding, we have worked with hundreds of extraordinary European founders, and have raised eight funds totalling more than $3bn.'), not used. Published inside quotation marks, as the firm's own words (Erik, 2026-09-26).

investment_stage.basis: the firm's own words: 'Balderton's early stage and growth funds allow us to invest from Seed to IPO'; the cards' round labels run from Pre-seed to Series E and Secondary; the landed distribution is restated in report.md

investment_geo.basis: the site's own location filter (UK 80, Germany 29, France 23, USA 19, Sweden 16, Denmark 8, Netherlands 6 and eleven more of 205 cards) and the firm's stated focus on European-founded companies: core Europe, other US (two-label cap)

investment_scope.basis: focus from the firm's own site sector tags on 217 base rows, crosswalked to data/taxonomy/focus.json (crosswalk in config.json), published above 12 companies. Scope type is the curated judgement carried in investor.json.

investment_range.basis: median: $14.0M, the median of 77 entry rounds the firm announced in its own posts with a stated size (sources/site/news.json; each post is the row's entry citation; non-USD sizes converted at the ECB rate of the post date; by stage Pre-Seed $5.7M over 5, Seed $6.0M over 17, Series A $18.0M over 37, Growth $60.8M over 18; rows in sources/site/entry-round-sizes.json). It is a round size, not a cheque size, and it covers 2014 to 2026 only, the years of the news archive. lower: documented seed entries of $1.2M to $1.5M (Dinghy, Riff, Rahko); upper: the firm's own words for its growth fund, 'between $25m and $50m per company' (post of 2021-06-10)

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's own companies, most recognised first (PRO-152, Erik 2026-09-24). Considered next: Darktrace, MySQL, GoCardless, Contentful, Yoox.

aum.basis: both ends: the sworn Form ADV Section 7.B(1) gross asset values of the firm's exempt reporting adviser, Balderton Capital (UK) LLP, CRD 160323, annual amendment of 2026-03-31 (IAPD PDF parsed with pypdf, sources/registers/adv-160323.json): sixteen private funds, $8,511,214,328 in all (Fund V $3,523,565,022; VIII $1,006,656,092; Growth II $782,760,448; Growth I $755,375,012; IX $686,508,419; VI $621,489,999; VII $486,531,418; Gaia Investments $235,132,134; IV $210,682,155; Liquidity I $177,512,060; six parallel and co-investment vehicles $25,001,569). An exempt reporting adviser files no Item 5.F, so the 7.B composite is the sworn figure (Creandum precedent). The firm's own site says $5.7bn raised; Wikipedia gives $7.0bn of assets. Both belong here, not in the range.

funds.basis: sizes from the firm's own announcements and press at the time: Growth II $685M and IX $615M (https://www.balderton.com/news/balderton-announces-1-3b-in-new-funds-to-back-europes-top-entrepreneurs-as-they-build-world-changing-businesses/); VIII $600M (https://www.balderton.com/news/balderton-raises-new-600m-early-stage-fund-to-back-europes-next-wave-of-breakout-tech/); Growth I $680M (https://www.balderton.com/news/balderton-capital-expands-launching-680m-early-growth-fund-to-invest-in-future-tech-giants-born-in-europe/); VII $400M (https://www.balderton.com/news/press-release-balderton-capital-europes-most-active-series-a-investor-launches-new-400m-early-stage-fund/); Liquidity I $145M (https://www.balderton.com/news/balderton-launches-europes-first-venture-fund-dedicated-to-providing-liquidity-to-early-stage-shareholders-in-high-growth-technology-companies/); VI $375M (https://www.balderton.com/news/press-release-balderton-doubles-down-on-europe-with-new-375m-fund/); V $305M (https://www.balderton.com/news/balderton-capital-raises-305m-series-a-venture-fund-to-invest-in-european-technology-start-ups-copy/); IV GBP 285M, reported as $430M (TechCrunch 2009, https://techcrunch.com/?p=2814); III EUR 430M, reported as $550M (TechCrunch 2006-11-16, https://techcrunch.com/2006/11/16/benchmark-capital-europe-raises-e430-million-2/); Benchmark Europe II $375M (Buyouts Insider, Jul 2004); Benchmark Europe I $750M at its close of May 2000 (Light Reading), cut to $500M in 2002. No entry carries an accession: the Luxembourg vehicles file their Form Ds before or during the raise. Not listed, counted here: the parallel 'A' vehicles, the 'EC' co-investment vehicles and Gaia Investments, S.L.P. (decisions.md D1, D6).

hq_location.basis: Principal office on the newest Form ADV: The Stables 28 Britannia Street, London, United Kingdom (BALDERTON CAPITAL, CRD 160323, Annual Amendment filed 2026-03-31). The firm's site lists London, United Kingdom; Berlin, Germany; Paris, France; Munich, Germany; the principal office is among them, so the site agrees. Rule (Erik 2026-09-24): the newest Form ADV principal office, unless the firm's own site disagrees, and then the site wins.
